findings.title: Manual shows the preset 'Automatic slow-down at an alert' (Gentle: pause) as working; nothing uses it
findings.detail: The difficulty parameter autoSlowDefault ('pause' on Gentle, 'slow' on the others) is only written to state.env.time.autoSlow (createGame.ts:108). Nothing reads that field; the only other mention is the setter in environment/timeCommands.ts:101. Auto-slow behaviour comes from AutoSlowWatcher, which reads settings.gameplay.autoSlowCritical / autoSlowWarning (Game.ts:137, default 'slow'), and those settings have no control on any screen. So choosing Gentle never pauses at a critical alert. Manual section 1.6 lists the row as in effect, which contradicts section 8 of the same manual (default: critical slows). The spec says nothing in the documents may describe a feature that does not work, and that a rule shown as working when it does not is to be listed as a wrong string. presetDisplay.ts has it in effect because it is missing from UNWIRED_PARAMS. To reproduce: grep -rn autoSlowDefault src (one consumer, createGame.ts:108), then grep -rn 'time.autoSlow' src (only the setter). Fix: in the manual, mark the row not in effect and say auto-slow follows the setting. Integrator: add autoSlowDefault to UNWIRED_PARAMS, or wire it to the watcher.

findings.title: Manual describes a 'focus line (top left)' and a minimap that the game does not have
findings.detail: Section 2 says 'The journal's focus line (top left) asks one question at a time ("Where is the ground sheltered, warm and diggable?")'. No HUD component shows aims: the files in src/ui/hud are AlertsFeed, ColonyPulse, ContextPrompts, PossessedPanel, SoundCuePips, TimeCluster and Toasts. The text for aim-find-site is used only by Journal > Aims (src/ui/panels/journal/AimsTab.tsx via timeline.ts aimLine) and by the hand-over banner. GDD 08 section 3.4 specifies the focus line at (16, 76) as T2, and it is not built. Section 12 also lists 'minimap' and 'focus line (auto, always, never)' as working settings. gameplay.minimap and gameplay.focusLine have no consumer: they are only mapped in src/ui/styles/prefs.ts, and no minimap component exists. To reproduce: grep -rn 'focusLine\|minimap' src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx outside src/game/settings and src/ui/screens/settings (only prefs.ts mappings). The implementer's own page.png shows only the time cluster at top left. Fix: say the aim is in Journal > Aims, and mark the Minimap and Focus line settings as having no effect in this build. Integrator: these are two more 'setting with no effect' cases, like auto-slow.

findings.title: DEVIATIONS misquotes GDD 06 for R2 and R20
findings.detail: R2's 'GDD says' column, and the section C row for GDD 06 section 5.13, say the hand-over specifies nothing about food. GDD 06 section 5.13 clause (c) does: 'the queen keeps her remaining reserves, split equally into GDD 02 reserve (C) and reserveP (P)'. The amendment should target that clause. The section C row for GDD 06 section 1.6 says Lasius starts 'around day 9'. The GDD table gives window 9..12 and default doy 10 (Summer 3). Day 9 was the earlier STATUS ruling of Nov 15, which is itself a deviation and has no row.

findings.title: Manual's 'Rival colonies' preset row does not match the screen text
findings.detail: The manual prints '1 young colonies nearby', '2 young colonies nearby' and '3 young colonies nearby'. The New Game screen prints '1 young rivals nearby' and so on. The manual says this table is generated from presetDisplay.ts, and acceptance 2 asks that it match the screen's data. In my script comparison against presetCard() this was the only one of 43 rows that differed. The row label 'Rival colonies' with values 1/2/3 also sits next to the rule table's 'Rival colonies' defaults 2/3/4 with no explanation that the row counts incipient foundations.

findings.title: Controls table lists a gamepad chord in the keyboard column (Photo mode)
findings.detail: '| Photo mode | F2 or LS+RS | RS+LS |'. keyboardOf() adds every ActionDef.fixed binding to the keyboard column whatever its kind, and photo-mode has a fixed pad chord p(RS, LS) (src/input/actions.ts:56). The manual copies the generator faithfully, but a player reads LS+RS as a keyboard key. Acceptance 2 asks that each control is in the bindings with that default, and LS+RS is not a keyboard/mouse binding. This is the generator's bug: list it as a wrong string for the content owner. docs/manual/02-controls.md:92 has the same row.

findings.title: Manual says every key can be rebound, but marker tools, undo and planner rotation are hard-coded
findings.detail: Shift+1 to Shift+7 (tool select), Ctrl+Z (undo) and, while the dig or entrance tool is active, Q/E (planner rotate) and Shift+wheel (resize) are read as raw key codes, not input actions. They cannot be changed in Settings > Controls and are not in the generated tables. The manual's section 6 table and section 3 should say these keys are fixed. With a tool active, Q/E rotate the plan, not the camera.

findings.title: Rule table shows '-' for preset values that the presets do set
findings.detail: presetRuleValues sets winterMode 'timelapse' for all three presets, extinctionEndsGame true for all three, foundingAssist true/true/false and queenSenescence false/false/true. The manual shows '-' in the Gentle/Naturalist/Harsh columns for all four. It is the right call that two of them are not in effect, but the presets do carry values. Also, the paragraph says 'seven rules marked on screen', while the table marks eight rows 'on screen' (Starting season, in the Locality column, is the eighth).

findings.title: The species URL flag accepts the three unavailable species
findings.where: docs/MANUAL.md:44; README.md URL flags table; src/game/newGame/options.ts:56
findings.detail: options.ts picks species from SPECIES_IDS with no availability check, so ?autostart=1&species=messor-barbarus starts a Messor game. The manual says 'Starting one by URL flag is not supported', and the README lists only lasius-niger. Better to say the flag accepts the other ids for testing but those species are not playable, so a maintainer is not surprised.
